task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Alder Reach's trial of earlier commercial waste collection in its restaurant district. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Alder Reach sanitation department will trial commercial waste collection between 8 and 10 p.m. in a 20-block restaurant district.
The district's participating businesses currently receive collection beginning around 2 a.m.; residential waste schedules are not part of the trial.
The six-week trial runs from Oct. 12 through Nov. 22, 2026, with collections on the same two nights each week.
Twenty-six of the district's 41 eligible businesses enrolled, and the other businesses will keep their existing collection arrangements.
The council authorised a $24,000 trial budget covering additional route staffing and temporary collection equipment.
Residents living above restaurants asked for an earlier schedule after repeatedly reporting overnight bottle-emptying noise.
The complaint log counts contacts rather than unique complainants, so it cannot establish how many separate residents objected.
Residents committee member Tavi Lorn said, "The truck arrives after the music has stopped, just when we think the street is finally settling down."
Restaurant operators raised a competing concern that waste carts could obstruct customers and outdoor service during the earlier window.
Restaurant operator Mera Voss said, "Eight o'clock is not the end of our working day; it is often the middle of it."
Participating businesses will use designated collection points in side lanes rather than placing carts beside outdoor tables.
The trial plan requires carts to be removed from those points after collection, rather than stored there throughout the night.
The sanitation department will record missed collections, blocked access reports and time spent on each route.
The department has not set a numerical noise-reduction target or supplied sound measurements from the current service.
Drivers will have a route marshal on the first two collection nights to identify problems at the shared pickup points.
A business may leave the trial after notifying the department, but it must make arrangements for its waste rather than assume an automatic extra pickup.
A review meeting with residents and enrolled businesses is planned after the third week.
Any permanent change will require a new council decision after the final report, not simply the completion of the trial.
The district's narrow service lanes were laid out before its current concentration of restaurants and outdoor dining areas.
The earlier route will not collect cooking oil, which remains covered by separate private arrangements.
The department will distribute a printed map of collection points to residents and businesses before the start date.
No trial outcomes are available, and the department has not claimed that earlier collection will resolve every source of nighttime noise.

forbidden_additions: A districtwide mandatory or permanent change.
Measured noise improvement or a unique-resident count inferred from complaint contacts.
A change to residential collection or cooking-oil service.
preserve: The two different busy periods experienced by residents and restaurants.
The limited enrolment, shared pickup points and later decision on permanence.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
